context:
Goal: stale-draft handling follows rules you made, not guessed numbers.
Problem (rule): decision stalled-steps says a draft over 12 h with no live lane is stale. No ruling of yours sets 12 h (R37: no hard fixed numbers), and the pass that used it closed 71 PRs whose work was not on main. That pass is stopped; closes now go only through runner 10 from the ledger.
Based on (ruling): R37; ruling pr-close-by-batch-runner (your 11:45 CST Nov 13 pick).
Departs from: main, where stalled-steps names 12 h — a removes the cutoff.
Meanwhile: nothing waits; PR 3159 files it as an unruled fixed number.

options.gain: No fixed number to defend; a draft's work decides, not its age.
options.how: Stale drafts are judged by the evidence ledger and runner 10's closes, with no hours cutoff.
options.label: Drop the 12 h cutoff (recommended)
options.lose: A quiet draft with no ledger row stays open until the ledger covers it.

options.gain: Old drafts surface on a schedule you chose.
options.how: You name the hours; the decision stalled-steps carries it as your ruling.
options.label: Keep a cutoff and set the number
options.lose: One more fixed number to maintain; today's 12 h came from no one's word.

reply: Settled, not a question: R37 and your 11:36 CST Nov 13 words ("these hard static time limits are not something i approve") already rule it. The 12 h cutoff is dropped; lane pr-close-record removes it in PR 3159. Coordinator 12:04 CST.

shown.label: Keep a cutoff and set the number

title: Should the 12 h stale-draft cutoff in decision stalled-steps be dropped, or ruled on?
why: A fixed number with no ruling needs your word or removal.
